title: Workshop topic group draft
prompt: A review workshop has 11 possible mini-topics and will choose 4 of them for a short practice set. The order of the chosen mini-topics does not matter. How many different practice sets can be chosen?

answer.explanation: This is an unordered selection, so use C(11,4).

hints: The order of the mini-topics does not matter.
Use a combination rather than a permutation.
Compute C(11,4).
solutionSteps: The task asks for an unordered group of 4 mini-topics from 11.
C(11,4) = 330, so there are 330 possible practice sets.

misconceptions.feedback: That counts different orders of the same 4 mini-topics. The prompt says the order does not matter.

title: Inspection station order draft
prompt: A lab dashboard has 8 inspection stations available. A supervisor will assign 3 different stations to first, second, and third positions in a morning checklist. How many ordered checklists are possible?

answer.explanation: This is an ordered arrangement of 3 distinct stations chosen from 8.

hints: The positions first, second, and third are different.
No station is repeated.
Multiply the descending number of choices for the three positions.
solutionSteps: There are 8 choices for the first position.
After that, 7 stations remain for the second position and 6 remain for the third position.
The number of ordered checklists is 8 * 7 * 6 = 336.

misconceptions.feedback: A combination ignores order. Here first, second, and third positions make order matter.

title: Sensor calibration alert draft
prompt: A device monitor flags 78% of sensors that need recalibration and 9% of sensors that do not. About 12% of sensors need recalibration. If a sensor is flagged, what is the probability that it needs recalibration?

answer.explanation: Compare flagged sensors that need recalibration with all flagged sensors.

hints: Find P(needs recalibration and flagged).
Find P(no recalibration needed and flagged).
Divide the first joint probability by the total probability of being flagged.
solutionSteps: The total probability of a flag is 0.0936 + 0.0792 = 0.1728.

misconceptions.feedback: The 78% value is P(flagged | needs recalibration), not P(needs recalibration | flagged). The base rate and false-flag rate both matter.

title: Workshop support request draft

answer.explanation: After conditioning on the online lab section, use only the 18 online students as the denominator.

hints: The phrase given that restricts the sample space.
Use the online lab count as the denominator.
Count only the online lab students who requested evening support.
solutionSteps: The condition says the student is in the online lab section, so the relevant denominator is 18.
Within that section, 7 students requested evening support.
The conditional probability is 7/18, which is about 0.3889.

title: Survey card follow-up draft
prompt: A folder has 16 survey cards, and 6 of them are marked for follow-up. A coordinator selects 5 cards without replacement. What is the probability that exactly 2 of the selected cards are marked for follow-up?

answer.explanation: Choose the 2 follow-up cards and the 3 non-follow-up cards, then divide by all groups of 5 cards.

hints: The selection is without replacement.
Choose the follow-up cards and the non-follow-up cards separately.
Divide by all possible groups of 5 selected cards.
solutionSteps: Choose exactly 2 of the 6 follow-up cards: C(6,2).
The other 3 selected cards must come from the 10 cards not marked for follow-up: C(10,3).
Divide by all possible groups of 5 cards: C(16,5).

misconceptions.feedback: A binomial model assumes the success probability stays constant. Here the cards are selected without replacement.
